Here's a quick lesson on how stocks work.
Company A wishes to sell shares of its company. To do so, Company A wishes to split its company into 1 million pieces.
Company A must now declare how much each shares will go for. This is known as an IPO (Initial Price Offer)
Once all shares have been sold, each individual owns a piece of the company, based on the number of "shares"
These shares are now considered a commodity, and its value is dependent on the people that own these.
However, if Company A does not actually make any income, the shares hold no actual value. Which will determine its P/E ratio also known as a "Price to Earnings Ratio" telling consumers how much they must spend for the company to go up 1 dollar. Generally, this is around 11-20 for good companies.
When the owners realize that the Company doesn't actually have an intrinsic value they usually end up selling their stocks, which when there are a large volume of sales causes it to become bearish and prices will drop. Eventually, if the company cannot meet the demands, it'll eventually go bankrupt.
So no, this is not a wise choice to go if there is no plan thought out for this. Look at what happened to that Thirsty Redshit.
